title: 1980 AHSME Problem 23
statement: Line segments drawn from the vertex opposite the hypotenuse of a right triangle to the points trisecting the hypotenuse have lengths \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x,\) where \(x\) is a real number such that \(0\lt x\lt\frac\pi2.\) The length of the hypotenuse is

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not uniquely determined by the given information

solutions.text:
Let the hypotenuse have endpoints \((0,0)\) and \((h,0),\) and let the right-angle vertex be \((u,v).\) The right-angle condition gives \(u^2+v^2=hu.\) The squared distances to \((\frac{h}{3},0)\) and \((\frac{2h}{3},0)\) sum to \[ \begin{aligned} &(u-\frac{h}{3})^2+v^2\\ &\quad+(u-\frac{2h}{3})^2+v^2 =\frac{5h^2}{9}. \end{aligned} \] This also equals \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.\) Hence \(h=\frac{3}{\sqrt5}=\frac{3\sqrt5}{5}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Put the hypotenuse on the \(x\)-axis and assign coordinates to the right-angle vertex
Add the squares of the two trisector-segment lengths so the unknown horizontal position cancels
